name: Freeze Out Dominoes
description: Freeze-Out Dominoes is a simple children's domino game similar to the card game War. Players arrange dominoes face-down in a line and reveal tiles in turn. The player whose tile matches one of the suits shown in a trick takes all revealed dominoes. It emphasizes chance over strategy, making it ideal for young players learning domino games.

history.origins: Freeze-Out Dominoes is a modern children's game modeled after the card game War. It was likely designed to teach young players the fundamentals of domino games and matching mechanics.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Freeze-Out emerges as an educational game for children.
1970s-Present: Included in children's domino game compilations and educational resources.
history.cultural: Primarily a family and educational game, used to teach children about domino matching, turn-taking, and basic luck-based gameplay.
history.evolution: Simplification of traditional domino rules to make the game accessible to young children while maintaining the core matching mechanic.

setup.dealing: Shuffle all dominoes face-down. Distribute evenly among players. If dominoes don't divide evenly, remove extras from play. Each player arranges their dominoes face-down in a horizontal line.

rules.objective: Be the first player to accumulate all dominoes by winning tricks.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Lead Tile**: One player reveals the rightmost domino in their line and announces its two suits (or single suit if a double). 2. **Other Players' Turns**: Each other player, in turn, reveals their rightmost domino. 3. **Trick Winner**: The player whose revealed domino matches one of the two suits from the lead tile wins all face-up dominoes (the 'trick'). 4. **Captured Tiles**: The trick winner places captured dominoes at the left end of their line, face-down. 5. **Next Round**: The trick winner leads the next round by revealing their new rightmost domino. 6. **Elimination**: Players who run out of dominoes exit the game. 7. **Game End**: The last remaining player with dominoes wins.
keyRules: Dominoes must be arranged face-down in a single horizontal line.
Players always reveal from the rightmost position in their line.
To win a trick, a domino must match one (or both) suits of the lead tile.
Captured dominoes are placed at the left of the line, face-down.
The trick winner always leads the next round.
Players eliminated when they have no dominoes left.
Extras not distributed during dealing are removed from play entirely.

strategy.basic: Pay attention to which suits have been played. Try to remember who has dominoes with matching suits. There is very little strategyâ€”the game is almost entirely luck-based.
strategy.intermediate: Watch the order of other players' dominoes in their lines. If you observe that a player's line is getting shorter on the left (where won dominoes are added), they may be winning tricks. Arrange your own won dominoes strategically by placing them in positions that favor future leads.
strategy.advanced: While primarily luck-based, skilled players can increase odds slightly by managing the positioning of won tiles. If you must arrange captured dominoes in your line, cluster matching suits together to improve your chances of holding matching tiles when needed. However, the random nature of face-down tiles limits advanced strategy.
tips: This is fundamentally a game of luck, not skill. Focus on entertainment rather than competitive advantage.
Young children learn domino matching and taking turns, which is the educational value of the game.
Play multiple rounds to give all players a chance to win, regardless of early luck.

variations.name: Highest Tile in Suit
variations.description: The lead player announces a single suit, and the trick is won by the highest-value domino in that suit among those revealed (not the first match).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes trick resolution only; engine overrides could be added when implementing highest-of-suit logic.

variations.name: Cumulative Score Variant
variations.description: Instead of playing until one player has all dominoes, play multiple rounds (5-10) and award 1 point per domino captured each round. Highest score after all rounds wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds targetScore and round count; overrides to be added when implementing scoring variant.

variations.name: Two-Player Freeze-Out
variations.description: Standard rules with just two players. Each draws 7-10 dominoes depending on preference.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes player count and hand size; engine supports 2-6 players and even deal already.

scoring.description: No points are explicitly scored. The game is won simply by accumulating all dominoes.
scoring.winCondition: First player to capture all dominoes wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A beginner-friendly domino game where players reveal tiles in turn and collect tricks by matching suits, perfect for children learning domino games.
